title: a sprint started in a long session pays that session's context on every turn
detail: stop-blocks-once, a trivial 18-minute change, measured 12.9M tokens. 11.6M were the main thread (Opus), 1.3M the three role agents. 10.4M came from session eb27f96e, which had already run the whole one-bash-lexer sprint, so every briefing/build/review turn re-read that context (98% cache reads). The same sprint in a fresh session was 2.5M. Candidate: sprint-start and each gate advance read the session's current context size (platform_adapter.read_usage) and warn above a threshold derived from transcripts, naming the hand-off path; tier report shows each sprint's peak context. Advisory, not a block.
